votes.question: On Motion to Concur in the Senate Amendments — An Act to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow early childhood educators to take the educator expense deduction, and for other purposes (H R 5334)
votes.plain_language: The House voted to accept the Senate's rewrite of H.R. 5334, which imposes Russia-related sanctions and tariffs, extends an Iran sanctions law, and also expands a teacher tax deduction to early-childhood educators. A Yea accepts that Senate version. A Nay rejects it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Resolution — Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran (H CON RES 93)
votes.plain_language: This resolution tells the President to remove U.S. forces from hostilities with Iran unless Congress authorizes it, except for forces needed to defend against an imminent attack if the President follows the War Powers Resolution's time limits. A Yea agrees. A Nay rejects it.

lobbying.bill_title: Directing the President, pursuant to section 5(c) of the War Powers Resolution, to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran

votes.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Whistleblower Protection Act (H R 4646)

votes.plain_language: The resolution would impeach President Trump over Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection practices that it says violate the Constitution. This vote was a motion to table, which kills the resolution. A Yea tables it; a Nay would have left it pending.

lobbying.bill_title: Impeaching Donald John Trump, President of the United States, for high crimes and misdemeanors.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.

stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.

Pete Hegseth’s DoD has been illegally scraping private medical records in an effort to force out transgender servicemembers.

The government shouldn’t be pawing through anyone’s private medical records – period.

I’m leading the charge alongside @RepDelBene and my fellow @EqualityCaucus co-chairs to stop this blatant overreach and hold Secretary Hegseth accountable.

When I got to Congress, I heard heartbreaking stories from folks across the country who couldn’t afford the insulin they needed to live – they were rationing their medicine or just going without. That’s why, in 2022, I wrote the bill that capped the cost of insulin at $35/month for Medicare recipients, worked to get bipartisan support for our proposal and got it signed into law.

We need to enact common-sense gun reform, and we needed to do it yesterday. How many lost lives is it going to take?

Today and every day, I stand with Minnesota’s Tribal communities.

posts.text: I’m proud to announce that my office secured more than $2.2 million in federal grants to hire firefighters for the Rosemount Fire Department! I also got word this week that the Lakeville, Shakopee and Woodbury Fire Departments will receive federal grants. Altogether, that’s more than $3.7 million back to fire departments in CD2! This funding will create jobs, protect our firefighters and help keep communities across Minnesota’s Second District safe.

October is LGBTQ+ history month, a chance for us to celebrate the brave folks who have stood up and fought for equal rights, protections and acceptance for our community. We’ve come a long way in this fight, but there’s still more work to do. Together, we’ll keep working toward a future where every Minnesotan can be who they are and love who they love. 🌈🩷

Cheryl and I are keeping the students, teachers and families impacted by last night’s shooting in Eden Prairie in our prayers today. 

No homecoming celebration should end with gun violence. We’ve got to do better for our kids and pass common sense gun control in this country.

Another disappointing jobs report. Unemployment ticked up to 4.2%, job growth slowed (again) and Minnesotans are feeling it.

President Trump promised a Golden Age — yet opportunities are dwindling, prices are rising and folks can’t keep up.

Minnesotans deserve better.

It’s that time of year! Every fall, I visit Mr. Snobeck’s political science class at Eagan High School to answer questions about our government and share my experience as an elected official.

I had a great time today hearing from and speaking to some of Eagan’s best and brightest.

It was an honor to receive the Mayor’s Award from Newport Mayor Laurie Elliott and the Newport City Council today. Serving Minnesota’s Second District is a true honor, and I couldn’t be more grateful for Mayor Elliott’s partnership over the years. Thank you, Mayor Elliott! https://t.co/C9FKuKa8I0

Hispanic Heritage Month is an opportunity to celebrate the achievements and contributions of Hispanic Minnesotans. This month and always, we celebrate the diversity and rich cultures that make our state stronger!
Cheryl and I got to visit the top of the Capitol Dome in Washington! It was a hike – literally 300 stairs – but I’d say the view was worth it. https://t.co/53Hkcc5CIZ

I’m thrilled, but not surprised, that the Lynx’s own Cheryl Reeve was named WNBA Coach of the Year (again!) and Olivia Miles was unanimously voted WNBA Rookie of the Year! 

Not only have these two had a historic, record-breaking season – they also led the Lynx to the top seed in the playoffs. Cheryl and Olivia, Minnesota couldn’t be prouder of you. 

P.S. Can’t wait to watch you take down the Liberty tonight!

I think we could all use a little Dakota pick-me-up right about now, or should I say... Da-Cow-Ta! 

What do you think of Dakota’s Halloween costume? My wife Cheryl has always wanted a Highland Cow. Dakota is not very amused. https://t.co/cV512SCWJc

Happy National Public Lands Day! 
From neighborhood playgrounds to national parks, our public lands are essential to our communities. Today, let’s commit to protecting these sacred outdoor spaces for generations of Minnesotans to come.🌲⛰️🛶🏕️

President Trump’s vanity projects are slated to cost over $1.8 billion of your tax dollars. That same amount of money could pay for: 

- 600+ million school lunches 
- 12 million Americans’ electric bills for one month 
- A full year of medical bills for 88,000 veterans 
- 27,000+ new firefighters or schoolteachers
- 35+ million tanks of gas for a typical sedan

Minnesotans want a life they can afford – not an algae-green Reflecting Pool and a ballroom built for billionaires.
